learning: Iteration 1 is the reference: progress 0.11/0.155/0.109 on oval/s-bend/slalom, line_loss 1 per run, max_error about 0.061-0.065 m. Iteration 3 showed that the lead is the limit below 4 cm. Oscillation has stayed in 0.065-0.155 in every iteration, so jitter is not the limit. If progress is unchanged and line losses remain at 1, the next test is a gain change (ki for the constant rms offset) or a 4 cm span at 16 mm. Lead stays at 4 cm.
notes: Single-variable package: the Builder's sensor_size 0.016 change on the iteration 1 geometry and controller, with no controller changes. This isolates footprint from gains.
rationale: The Builder's geometry tests only sensor_size (0.012 to 0.016 m) on the iteration 1 layout, which is the best design so far (score 51.27, s-bend progress 0.155). Iteration 3 showed that a 2 cm lead collapses s-bend progress to 0.04, so the lead stays at 4 cm. Iteration 2 showed that a 16 mm footprint with a wider span removed line losses but did not stop the off-track exits. The controller is therefore kept exactly as in iteration 1 (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.6, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction line loss), so any change in the race is attributable to the footprint. I expect line_loss_events to fall toward 0 and max_error to stay near 0.06 m. This is a prediction, not a measurement. The rms_error near 0.03 on every track suggests a steady offset (likely motor mismatch), which the controller has not yet addressed; I am not adding integral action in this single-variable test.
